title: VM 106 (palworld-server): take its address from the router (DHCP) so the router app can reserve it
description:
Learned on ADD4 (2026-10-10): the operator's Spectrum router app only lets a device be reserved — and so port-forwarded — when the router itself leased its address. The operator has reserved 192.168.1.44 for VM 106's MAC BC:24:11:E8:9F:7A and forwarded UDP 8211 to it (ADD152).

Measured 2026-10-11: VM 106's address is set by Proxmox cloud-init — `qm config 106` has `ipconfig0: ip=192.168.1.106/24,gw=192.168.1.1` — and cloud-init rewrites /etc/netplan/50-cloud-init.yaml from it at every boot. The first run of this step edited that file; the host restarted at 02:13 and VM 106 came back on 192.168.1.106.

On the Proxmox host: set VM 106 to take its address by DHCP at the source (`qm set 106 --ipconfig0 ip=dhcp`), regenerate its cloud-init drive (`qm cloudinit update 106`), and restart VM 106 so cloud-init applies it (`qm reboot 106`; the Palworld service starts on boot). Keep every other setting of VM 106 as it is.

Done when `qm config 106` shows `ipconfig0: ip=dhcp` and `qm guest exec 106 -- ip -4 addr show eth0` shows inet 192.168.1.44 with `dynamic`.
